pharm: Hygroscopic keratolytic and humectant; osmotic diuretic at high IV doses (specialist)
quick: Topical: apply to affected skin/nail 1-2 times daily
Topical use acceptable; avoid breast/nipple area
summary: Urea is most commonly used as a topical keratolytic and emollient (humectant) for dry, rough, thickened, or hyperkeratotic skin conditions and for debridement and softening of damaged or ingrown nails. Lower concentrations hydrate and soften skin, while higher concentrations (around 40%) are keratolytic and aid debridement of hyperkeratotic lesions and dystrophic nails. Note: 'Urea' is a broad/context-dependent entry - the same molecule is also used historically as an osmotic agent and is a measured serum metabolite; this record focuses on the common FDA-labeled topical use. Always confirm the specific product strength and indication.
indications: Debridement and promotion of normal healing of hyperkeratotic surface lesions, especially where healing is retarded by local infection, necrotic tissue, fibrinous/purulent debris, or eschar
Treatment of hyperkeratotic conditions: dry, rough skin, dermatitis, psoriasis, xerosis, ichthyosis, eczema, keratosis pilaris/palmaris, keratoderma, corns and calluses
Treatment of damaged, ingrown, and devitalized nails

dosage.d: Apply to affected skin twice per day, or as directed; rub in until completely absorbed
dosage.n: Higher strengths are keratolytic; use on affected areas only

dosage.d: Apply to the diseased/damaged nail(s) twice per day, or as directed
dosage.n: Softens dystrophic nail to aid removal/debridement

dosage.d: Apply to dry skin one to two times daily
dosage.n: Hydrating/humectant effect for xerosis and ichthyosis

admin: Apply to affected skin or nail and rub in until completely absorbed
Use on intact or appropriately prepared skin; avoid eyes, lips, and mucous membranes unless directed
Match the concentration to the intended effect (lower = emollient, higher = keratolytic)
Discontinue and reassess if irritation occurs
For external use only unless a specific product directs otherwise
moa: Urea is hygroscopic and acts as a humectant, drawing and binding water in the stratum corneum to hydrate and soften skin. At higher concentrations it is keratolytic, disrupting the bonds between keratinocytes and dissolving the intercellular matrix of hardened keratin, which loosens hyperkeratotic tissue and dystrophic nail and promotes debridement and re-epithelialization.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to any of the listed ingredients
relative: Application to open wounds, broken or inflamed skin unless directed
Use near eyes or mucous membranes
monitor: Local skin irritation or allergic reaction

preg: Topical urea is generally considered acceptable in pregnancy given minimal systemic absorption. Use as directed by a clinician.
lact: Topical urea is generally acceptable during breastfeeding; avoid applying to the breast or nipple area to prevent infant exposure.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed for topical use. (High-dose intravenous urea, a specialist osmotic use, would require renal assessment but is outside common topical use.)
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed for topical use.

minor: Other topical agents on the same area - urea can enhance penetration of co-applied topicals
interactions.diagnostics: No laboratory interference from topical use.

common: Local burning or stinging on application
emergency: Severe allergic reaction with swelling or breathing difficulty (rare)

monitoring: Skin or nail response to treatment
Local tolerance - irritation, burning, or rash
counsel: Apply only to the affected skin or nail and rub in fully
Some mild stinging can occur, especially on cracked skin or at higher strengths
Avoid getting it in the eyes, lips, or on healthy surrounding skin
Stop and tell your doctor if you develop a rash or worsening irritation
Use the strength your clinician recommended - higher strengths are for thick or hardened skin/nails
pk: Softening/hydration over days of regular use
Acts locally; not characterized systemically for topical use
Not applicable for topical use (minimal absorption)
Local effect during the application period
Store per product labeling at room temperature; keep container closed
pearls: Group/context-dependent entry: 'Urea' covers topical keratolytic/emollient products (FDA-labeled), and the same molecule is a serum metabolite and a specialist osmotic agent - confirm the product and indication
Effect is concentration-dependent: low strengths hydrate (emollient), high strengths (~40%) are keratolytic
Useful adjunct to soften dystrophic nails and thick plaques and to enhance penetration of co-applied topicals
Minimal systemic absorption with topical use, so it is well tolerated
Avoid eyes and mucous membranes; main adverse effect is local irritation
missed: If a topical application is missed, apply it as soon as remembered and continue the regular schedule. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.
overdose: Overdose is very unlikely with topical use given minimal systemic absorption; excess application may cause local irritation - wipe off and resume normal use. If a large amount is ingested, provide supportive care and contact a poison control center. (High-dose intravenous urea is a specialist osmotic therapy with its own monitoring and is not the topical product described here.)
